### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e3bdc748841f8ec72aedc3d795227273f25c6baa` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `732a70f41808a42172a9ec25f88c68c330796bf8` — the merge of head `61188fd276bf5b55b2e2aa7c403b8d6ee740b6bc` into base `e3bdc748841f8ec72aedc3d795227273f25c6baa`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 732a70f41808a42172a9ec25f88c68c330796bf8 && git checkout 732a70f41808a42172a9ec25f88c68c330796bf8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e3bdc748841f8ec72aedc3d795227273f25c6baa 61188fd276bf5b55b2e2aa7c403b8d6ee740b6bc && git checkout -B drift-repro e3bdc748841f8ec72aedc3d795227273f25c6baa && git merge --no-ff 61188fd276bf5b55b2e2aa7c403b8d6ee740b6bc

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e3bdc748841f8ec72aedc3d795227273f25c6baa
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c5dee3126d16a8498dbdaa97faf881cbf2ac3c72`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/agent.zod.ts, skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-ai/evals/skills-tools-knowledge.json + none
Security-touching: yes

Inputs: card #37850 (body, 3 comments), PR #38156 (body, 4 files, net diff against `main` 581ae76a), the check-runs on the head. Read outside the diff, not reviewed: `packages/spec/src/shared/retired-key.ts`, `packages/spec/src/ai/agent-model-provider-retirement.test.ts`, `packages/qa/scenarios/src/skill-evals/grade.ts`, `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`, and the head of open PR #38013 (5bc3ee1a). No file in the diff implements the `hits`: the fourth file is the changeset. Check-runs read at 2026-11-28T04:44Z.

`Security-touching: yes` because the eval hunks for cases 6 and 7 change how answers about who may approve or confirm an action are graded. The SKILL.md and jsdoc hunks teach no such behaviour.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set: unchanged. Right.** The `agent.zod.ts` hunk is three jsdoc lines on the `provider` tombstone; the shape, `retiredKey(MODEL_PROVIDER_RETIRED)` and the `acceptRetiredDefaultResidue(…, MODEL_PROVIDER_RETIRED_KEY_RESIDUE)` wrap are byte-identical.
- **Public surface: the published skill text and the `.d.ts` jsdoc. Right.** No export, type or schema description (`.describe()`) changes; the jsdoc sits on a shape key, not in a `describe` string.
- **Eval catalog: three cases regraded, no prompt changed. Right** as a description of the diff (judged in ④).
- **Gates.** Concluded `success` on this head: Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Flag docs affected by code changes, PR-body guards, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check PR Size. Still `in_progress` at the reading above, so NOT yet a verdict: Build Core, the Type Check family (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger), the Lint family (ESLint, repo and tooling gates, docs and code guards, CI/release/engine gates, the two scoped lints), Test Core 1-10/10, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI. The dev's local exits are not a substitute. S1 below moves the head, so the delta record reads those families on the new head.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/skills` patch and `@objectstack/spec` patch: right. The skills catalog ships `skills/**`, and the spec change is a comment that reaches consumers only through the declaration files. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` match the diff on the PR body and in the changeset: nothing an author can write is accepted or refused differently. Check Changeset is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty. Nothing to answer.
- Dev's out-of-scope note (case 2 still passes `provider:'anthropic'` with no space, or a trailing-space or commented line): accepted as left open; see N1 for the opposite direction.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. No query, id materialisation or join in the diff.
- **Open PR #38013 — the two PRs do not conflict in text or in teaching, but they do not fit together under the token ceiling.** The hunks are disjoint (#38013: the knowledge-service sentence at `SKILL.md:244` and case 14; this PR: Model Configuration and cases 2, 6, 7), an in-memory merge of the two heads is clean, and neither sentence bears on the other. But #38013 re-pins `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` to 6906 AT its own measurement (27650 bytes), and this PR adds 3 bytes inside the 3-byte slack of today's 6893 row (27596 to 27599). Merged, the file is 27653 bytes: `ceil((27653 - 27) / 4)` = 6907, one over #38013's row. The claim's serial note ("whichever lands second merges `main`") is therefore not enough: the second lander goes red on the token ratchet and must cut 2 bytes or re-pin. Not a defect of this head; a landing-order fact for the seat. The S1 fix below is byte-neutral and does not change this arithmetic.
- Box 3 of the card (the cite at `SKILL.md:457`) is closed without an edit. Confirmed on `main`: the only `agent.zod.ts` line cite left in the file is `:365`. That cite is S1.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/ai/agent.zod.ts` (jsdoc).** Holds against the code. `acceptRetiredDefaultResidue` strips a key only when its value is strictly equal to the captured literal, ahead of the closed shape; every other value reaches the untouched tombstone. The retirement test pins all three legs: `'openai'` parses and the output carries no `provider`; `'OpenAI'`, `'openai '`, `'anthropic'` and the rest are refused with the prescription; `z.input` stays `never`, so `tsc` refuses the key whatever its value. "One value parses … `tsc` refuses it all the same" is exact.

**`skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` (Model Configuration).** The new sentence — retired and refused, except the `'openai'` an 18.x toolchain wrote out, which parses and is stripped; delete it — agrees with the same code, and the instruction is unchanged. The four deletions that pay for it lose nothing a reader needs: "never a provider" is restated by the clause that follows and by the next sentence; "Outside 0–2 is a parse error" carries the bound that `min(0).max(2)` spelled; "free-string name" in the `model` row is unambiguous; "for the environment" narrowed a default the reader cannot set from metadata anyway.

S1 (should-fix) — the PR makes the section's own line cite stale. `SKILL.md:365` cites `packages/spec/src/ai/agent.zod.ts:87-95` for the `model` block's keys. On `main` that range is exactly `provider` (87) through `topP` (95). The jsdoc hunk adds two lines above them, so on this head the keys are `:89-97`, and `:87-95` now opens on two comment lines and stops at `temperature`, dropping `maxTokens` — one of the two keys the sentence is about. This is the defect class box 3 of this card exists for, re-introduced by the PR in the same file. Fix: `87-95` becomes `89-97` (byte-neutral, the ceiling holds), or keep the jsdoc at its old line count.

**`skills/objectstack-ai/evals/skills-tools-knowledge.json`.** Judged against each prompt, the skill text and the literal, case-sensitive grader.
- Case 2: `expected_output` now says "refused", matching the skill. The nine forbidden spellings only narrow what passes; no wrong answer gains a pass.
- Case 6: `refuses` is an inflection of a token already in the group; the wrong answer is still caught by `pendingActions.approve(`. No new wrong pass that `refused` did not already allow.
- Case 7: the any-of group is the four case and contraction spellings of the phrase `SKILL.md:212` teaches; the three hard tokens and both forbidden tokens are unchanged. No wrong answer gains a pass.
- Verdict on box 4 (grading token wrong, teaching right): agreed for both cases on the skill text. The recorded-round re-grade the PR reports was not re-run here and is not relied on.

Nits, no effect on the contract:
- N1 (nit) — case 2's two `}` spellings fail a correct answer that warns inline with the braces (the retired key shown inside a backticked `model: { … }`), which the old single token passed. The PR body's "the inline warning still passes" is true of the bare-key form only. The card's own note (a counter-example line fails the case) stays open for fenced examples.
- N2 (nit) — case 7 still misses a correct answer that uses a typographic apostrophe, "never retry", or bold inside the phrase.
- N3 (nit) — case 6's any-of group is met by generic refusal wording, so the case leans on its one forbidden call spelling. Older than this PR.

Open on this head: S1. No must-fix.
